page: Microsoft Azure F48amds_v7 is a memory-intensive server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 5669 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU workloads, as demonstrated by stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads and large-block uncached writes scoring in the top tier, while uncached large-block reads rank in the top 25%. The server exhibits strong performance in database operations, with Redis SET operations exceeding 130 million operations per second. However, a performance tradeoff is visible in large-scale machine learning tasks; while LLM inference speeds for small and medium models rank in the top tier, prompt processing and text generation for large 70B models fall into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F48amds_v7 offers high resource density by combining dedicated high-frequency compute cores with a substantial memory footprint and large local NVMe storage. This eliminates the need to provision separate high-speed storage volumes for data-intensive tasks. The hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput Redis caching layers, data compression pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
